prompt: A 65-year-old male with a history of chronic kidney disease presents to the clinic for his routine follow-up. He reports feeling more fatigued than usual but denies any symptoms of pain or acute distress. Laboratory tests are performed, which reveal a serum calcium level of 7.8 mg/dL and an albumin level of 2.8 g/dL. His physician notes that his albumin level is lower than the standard normal albumin level of 4.0 g/dL. Given the low albumin, the physician decides to calculate the corrected calcium level to guide potential treatment options. What is this patient's corrected calcium level?

rubric_items.text: Computes the albumin-corrected calcium as 8.76 mg/dL (±0.1).
